answer: Sybil tax blocks fake identities: each new identity pays a sunk 50-credit fee before trading. An agent selling ocean forecasts pays once and keeps its reputation. A second identity tracking a comet pays another 50 credits, never refunded. Making 1,000 fakes costs 50,000 credits, more than the diluted rewards they could split. An honest agent tending a garden schedule pays only once and keeps full, undiluted fees, so honesty stays cheapest.
